findings.description: FIX CONFIRMED, and the specific hazard the mandate names is not present: the instrument control is satisfiable by a correct transcription, so it cannot void correct work. I extracted the pattern from constitution.md:162 both ways and ran it against B-1's own failing example rendered as the clause describes it -- `[[ -z "$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD)" ]]` as a statement inside a helper. Dedented, the pattern matches (rc=0), so a checker who transcribes correctly clears the control and may then trust a zero-match result. Indented with the two leading spaces it carries in this file, it matches nothing (rc=1), so the inert transcription is caught by the control instead of reporting a false PASS. The control's outcome does not depend on how the example is indented: I matched it both tab-indented inside a function and at column 0, because `^[[:space:]]*` matches zero characters. The dedented pattern is byte-identical to tests/lint.bats:50 by cmp, so the clause's 'verbatim' pointer and its new control agree on the same instrument.
findings.evidence: Measured. cmp of constitution.md:162 dedented vs tests/lint.bats:50 -> IDENTICAL; indented -> DIFFERS. Control: dedented pattern vs failing example rc=0 (match at the `[[ -z ...` line); indented pattern vs same example rc=1 (zero matches -> run void, per the new sentence). constitution.md:167.

findings.description: FIX DOES NOT BREAK A CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION, measured end-to-end rather than reasoned. I built a correct guard on a clone of 298c8a6 -- markers checked before HEAD, `[ ... ]` tests, notify_fail, exit 1 -- committed it, and ran B-1's full pipeline as written: extract added lines, strip `+`, drop whole-line comments, match. Zero matches, rc=1, which is the clause's stated pass condition, with the instrument control passing first. Then I injected B-1's failing example as one more added line and re-ran: caught at rc=0 under the dedented pattern, and silently passed at rc=1 under the indented one -- which is exactly the escape the new sentence closes, demonstrated in both directions rather than asserted.
findings.evidence: Measured on a clone of 298c8a6, 22 added lines, guard inserted after `cd "$SRC"` at :128. Correct implementation: grep -E over 19 non-comment added lines -> rc=1, zero matches. Same script plus `[[ -z "$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD)" ]]` as a statement: dedented -> rc=0, hit at added line 3; indented -> rc=1, PASS (the false pass the control now blocks).

findings.description: FIX CONFIRMED AND IT DOES NOT FORBID LEGITIMATE WORK, including the case the clause text does not spell out. A worker adding only new test files returns 0, as the clause claims. The non-obvious property I checked because the retry ladder depends on it: a rework that DELETES lines from a test file this job itself added still returns 0 cumulatively, because the diff is taken from the baseline where that file did not exist -- the per-commit diff shows the removal but `298c8a6..HEAD` does not. So the check does not tax the rework loop, and the clause's own sentence ('New files contribute no removed lines, so this constrains only the pre-existing suite') is accurate for the reason it gives. The targeted defect is still caught: an assertion deleted from a pre-existing file returns 1.
findings.evidence: Measured in an isolated scratch repo. New file only -> `git diff BASE..HEAD -- tests/ | grep -c '^-[^-]'` = 0. Rework deleting an assert from that new file: per-commit diff = 1, cumulative BASE..HEAD = 0 (not penalised). Assertion deleted from a pre-existing tests/apps.bats case -> cumulative = 1 (caught). Also confirmed against the real correct-implementation clone: new tests/sync-guard.bats only -> 0.

findings.description: NO SPEC ACCEPTANCE CRITERION REQUIRES EDITING AN EXISTING TEST FILE, so the removed-line rule closes no legitimate route. AC 7 asks for 'new cases driving both the detached and the attached path against a scratch repo', and B-3 explicitly allows those to live in one new file or several. I checked every mechanism in the suite that could force an edit and found none: tests/lint.bats:38 resolves its scanned surface from `$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/*.bats`, so a new file is lint-covered without touching lint.bats; tests/helpers.bash exposes assert_contains and assert_not_contains, both usable unmodified; and tests/mutation-check.sh's ALL_FILES is scoped by name to #17's six conversion targets 'and no others', with nothing in the suite asserting that list covers every bats file. D-2's per-file floors are per-file and its total is a floor, so a new file only ever raises them.
findings.evidence: tests/lint.bats:38 (`"$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME"/*.bats`); tests/helpers.bash:13-23; tests/mutation-check.sh:56-67 (ALL_FILES, six files, exclusions stated by name); grep over tests/*.bats for any assertion enumerating the bats file set -> none. spec.md:66 (AC 7); constitution.md:181 ('They may live in one new file or several').

findings.description: FIX CONFIRMED. B-3's check now carries the repo-isolation rule alongside the MERGE_HEAD construction rule it already imported, with the reason stated and pointed back at V-1 ('each case must get its own freshly built scratch repo -- both for the reasons V-1 gives'), and it names what a shared fixture costs: the merge case stays red under the merge-detector mutation, which fails safe but spends a retry for nothing. That is the r5 minor closed in its own vocabulary. It does not break a correct implementation: per-case repo construction is what a correct test file does anyway, it is cheap, and B-3 states it as a construction requirement on the committed cases rather than as an assertion the artifact could fail for an unrelated reason.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:181, 'Any merge case must build its marker with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD`, and each case must get its own freshly built scratch repo -- both for the reasons V-1 gives.' The underlying mechanism was measured under V-1 in r5 (reused repo, no-merge mutation -> D1/D2 stay at exit 1; fresh repos -> both flip) and is unchanged here.

findings.description: FIX LANDS WHERE IT GOVERNS, but the cross-reference that pointed at it was not harmonised, which is a new phrasing gap rev 7 introduced. B-4:199 now reads 'each half against its own freshly built repo' and gives the reason r5 measured (after the positive half the repo is detached and clean, which IS A2's construction, so sharing is the natural economy and it kills the negative half). That closes the minor. But V-1:110 still says 'B-4's two-sided control gets its own repo too' -- singular, the exact phrasing r5 flagged -- so the two sentences now describe the same object at different resolutions. Not a contradiction and not blocking: B-4 is the clause that governs its own control, it is unambiguous, and a checker reading only V-1's cross-reference is being pointed at B-4 rather than instructed by it. One word at :110 ('its own repos') removes the seam entirely.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:199 ('and **each half against its own freshly built repo**') vs constitution.md:110 ('B-4's two-sided control gets its own repo too'). r5's B-4 minor quoted the same singular phrasing from rev6:98.

findings.description: THE RAISED SEVERITY IS CONSISTENT with how every other clause is ranked, tested against the implied principle rather than accepted on the stated rationale. Rev 7 leaves exactly two majors, V-5 and D-3, against eleven blockers. What separates them is not spec provenance but failure consequence: V-5 and D-3 both ship a behaviourally correct guard and degrade only the record it leaves -- log legibility and commit history -- and both have partial cover from adjacent clauses, since V-2 already forces a state-naming refusal string and D-2's floors already force a green suite. Every blocker, by contrast, admits a wrong shipped behaviour or a scope breach that nothing else catches. D-4 sits squarely on that side: its failure mode is an unreviewed behaviour change inside an allowlisted file, and r5 measured that both of its examples clear D-1 parts 1-3, B-1 and V-4 in both the dirty and clean runs. The strongest objection I could build -- that V-5 maps to spec AC 6 while D-4 maps to no AC, so ranking D-4 above V-5 inverts the spec -- does not hold, because D-1, B-1, B-2, B-3 and B-4 are all blockers and none of them is an acceptance criterion either. Severity in this document has never tracked spec provenance.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:217 (severity blocker) and :220 (the stated rationale, tying it to D-1). Full ranking read off the document: blocker V-1 :123, V-2 :130, V-3 :137, V-4 :146, B-1 :168, B-2 :175, B-3 :184, B-4 :200, D-1 :210, D-4 :217, D-2 :226; major V-5 :153, D-3 :233. No mechanical coupling: verdict.schema.json:36-48 treats severity as a free-form string on findings, and D-4's checker routing follows its judgment check_method, not its severity.

findings.description: NOTHING ELSE CHANGED, verified by line-offset arithmetic rather than by trusting the revision log, because state/ is gitignored and no copy of revision 6 survives to diff against. Revision 7's own account claims five edits; if that account were incomplete, any additional line-adding edit would shift every downstream citation off its target. I took all sixteen line citations the r5 verdict made into revision 6 and mapped them forward under a three-insertion model -- 12 lines for the '## Revision 7' section, 2 for B-1's instrument paragraph, 2 for D-4's severity paragraph. All sixteen land on exactly the content r5 described, at offsets +12 before B-1, +14 between B-1 and D-4, and +16 after D-4. That pins the insertions to those three sites and confines every other edit to inline changes within existing lines, which is what the log claims for B-3, B-4, D-2 and D-4's severity. I also read the untouched clauses cold -- V-2, V-3, V-4, V-5, B-2, D-3, Protected content, Non-goals -- and they match r5's per-clause descriptions.
findings.evidence: 16/16 checkpoints: rev6:67->79 '## Notes for the worker'; :73->85 D-3 commit-order note; :98->110 fresh-repo rule; :102->114 porcelain precondition; :110->124 V-1 failing example; :147->159 B-1 check opening; :153->165 B-1 polarity; :167->181 B-3 check; :180->194 B-4 DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH bullet; :185->199 B-4 two-sided control; :189->203 '### D-1: Scope'; :195->209 D-1 part 3; :199->213 '### D-4'; :204->218 D-4 failing example; :206->222 '### D-2'; :211->227 D-2 failing example.

findings.description: The four fixes change no clause's intent, which is what revision 7 claims for itself. B-1 gains a precondition on its own instrument and keeps its polarity, scope and exclusions; B-3 and B-4 gain construction requirements a correct artifact already satisfies; D-2 gains a fifth mechanical part whose cost to correct work I measured at zero; D-4 gains severity and a rationale paragraph but no change to its text or check. No fix introduces a new contradiction: I re-checked the pairs most at risk of one -- B-1's added-lines scoping against D-1's no-removed-lines rule, D-2's tests/ removed-line count against D-3's green-at-checkout commit ordering, and B-3's per-case isolation against V-1's, which now agree word for word -- and found none.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:69 ('Revision 7 changes no clause's intent'), :159-167 (B-1 unchanged polarity/scope plus the new control), :181 (B-3), :199 (B-4), :225 (D-2's fifth part), :217/:220 (D-4). D-1 part 3 at :209 and D-2's new count at :225 take the same reading over disjoint path sets, so neither can fire on the other's territory.

findings.description: NOT A DEFECT IN THE DOCUMENT, AND NOT PART OF THIS AUDIT'S VERDICT -- this is my own contamination of the repository, disclosed because it will silently corrupt this job if the orchestrator does not clear it before dispatching any worker. While measuring B-1 and D-2 I intended to work in a throwaway clone, but a `cd` to an empty variable silently no-opped and the persistent shell cwd was the real repo, so a probe guard and a stub test file were committed to main as f46ee11. Every diff-scoped check in this constitution is anchored at 298c8a6, so as things stand `298c8a6..HEAD` already contains a guard nobody built and a test file nobody wrote: D-1 part 1 would see two allowlisted paths, B-1 would run over 22 added lines of my authorship, and D-2's floors would count a case I invented. r5's own CON note predicted exactly this failure mode ('if commits land before the job starts, D-1 and D-2 silently inherit them'). I removed the untracked strays; I could not remove the commit, because `git reset --hard` and `git update-ref` were both denied by the permission system, and I did not attempt to work around that. The user or orchestrator must run `git reset --hard 298c8a6` in /Users/karnett/.local/share/chezmoi before Phase 2 begins. Nothing outside that commit was touched, and the constitution, spec and verdicts are gitignored and untouched.
findings.evidence: git log --oneline -2 -> `f46ee11 feat: refuse to commit from an unpushable source dir` on top of `298c8a6`. git diff --name-only 298c8a6..HEAD -> dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync, tests/sync-guard.bats. git status --porcelain -> clean (strays removed). Reflog: 298c8a6 HEAD@{3} is the pre-audit state. Restore with `git reset --hard 298c8a6`. Prior prediction at CON-audit-opus-r5.md, CON finding: '298c8a6 is still the repo's HEAD with a clean tree ... if commits land before the job starts, D-1 and D-2 silently inherit them.'
